title: Escape room game where you are trapped — Synthetic gameplay generated with Veo 3
author: MusicalMadnes
selftext:
Could AI be used to generate complex level designs that feel open world? 

How can in game AI prompting create novel mechanics for the user?

All clips generated to look like gameplay, and do not currently have any real playability.

comments.author: Katwazere
comments.body:
5 years on the models, currently the best ones either mess it up or are way to high poly. 2-3 on textures to a OK level.

Programming 2-3 years as the c's(c++ and c#) is a bit behind stuff like python and html and anything like that will need unity or unreal.

Level design itself, 20-30 years. I've yet to see anything that can produce stuff to even beginner level as it fundamentally doesn't get the basics of level design for gameplay and functionality.

comments.author: phoenix_bright
comments.body:
EA did a demo that does everything you’re talking about like 2 years ago.

And also, what is “synthetic gameplay”? This is an AI video not synthetic gameplay

replies.author: MusicalMadnes
replies.body: Link to demo? By synthetic gameplay, I mean using video generation tools to mimic gameplay logic, basically creating a prototype/concept art

comments.author: thedeadcircle
comments.body: Ahhh yes, the escape room classics are all here. Punching a window frame, making a window explode by slightly lifting a chair and being too tall for the office.
